graders.name: 01-detects-object-authz-finding
graders.graderMarkdown:
Is there a finding, of severity High or Critical (skill format) or category
`demonstrated vulnerability` (agent format), that identifies the export
handler's ownership check as broken because it verifies ownership of
`req.session.defaultNoteId` (via `findByIdAndOwner`) instead of the note
actually fetched and returned, `req.params.id` (via `findById`) — so the
check passes for any authenticated caller regardless of which note id they
request, letting them export any other user's note by id?

graders.name: 01-detects-object-authz-finding
graders.evidence:
## Scope
- Change reviewed: `src/api/notes.ts`, `src/repo/notes.ts` (diff `main..feat/notes-export`)
- Boundaries touched: authenticated HTTP route (`requireSession`), per-user note records
- Not covered: `requireSession` middleware implementation itself, `db.notes` driver internals, and any other consumer of `repository.findById`/`findByIdAndOwner` outside this diff (not shown)

## Findings
### HIGH: Note export checks ownership of the wrong resource, exposing any note's contents
- Category: demonstrated vulnerability
- Confidence: high — the mismatch is visible directly in the diff; no execution was performed
- Source: `fixtures/diff.md:29-30` (route body) — `req.params.id`, the target note id, supplied by any authenticated caller
- Path: `GET /notes/:id/export` (`fixtures/diff.md:29`) → `repository.findById(req.params.id)` (`fixtures/diff.md:33`, unfiltered lookup by id in `src/repo/notes.ts:15-17`) → authorization check at `fixtures/diff.md:38` calls `repository.findByIdAndOwner(req.session.defaultNoteId, req.session.userId)` — this verifies ownership of the caller's own signup-default note, not of `note` (the note fetched at line 33 and returned at line 42) → `res.send(note.body)` (`fixtures/diff.md:42`)
- Sink: `fixtures/diff.md:33,42` — `db.notes.findOne({ id })` with no owner filter, response body sent to caller
- Mitigation present: `fixtures/diff.md:38-39` (`ownerNote` check) — insufficient because it validates a different object than the one being served. It always evaluates the same true/false outcome for a given caller regardless of which note id was requested, so it never blocks access to another user's note.
- Attacker and gain: any authenticated caller (holder of a valid session, `req.session.userId` set) obtains the full body of any note whose UUID they know or enumerate, including notes owned by other accounts — a full object-level authorization bypass (IDOR)
- Scenario: Caller A authenticates and calls `GET /notes/<B's note UUID>/export`. `findById` returns B's note. The authorization check only confirms A owns A's own default note (`req.session.defaultNoteId` belongs to A, so `ownerNote` is truthy). The response sends B's note body to A. The UUID format check at line 30 does not gate on ownership, only on shape.
- Mitigation: replace the ownership check with `repository.findByIdAndOwner(req.params.id, req.session.userId)` — i.e. verify ownership of the note actually being fetched/exported, matching the pattern already used correctly in the sibling `DELETE` route (`fixtures/diff.md:50`)
- Verification: add a test where user A requests `/notes/:id/export` for a note owned by user B and assert a 403/404; add a positive test where A exports A's own non-default note and assert 200 with the correct body
- Reported by: claude

## Hypotheses requiring investigation
- Whether `defaultNoteId` is ever attacker-influenced (e.g., settable via another endpoint) — not resolved from this diff; if a caller could set their own `defaultNoteId`, that still would not fix the export flaw above but would matter for other flows referencing it. Next verification: locate where `req.session.defaultNoteId` is assigned.
- Whether `db.notes.findOne`/`deleteOne` perform any implicit tenant scoping at the driver/ORM level (e.g., a global query middleware) that isn't visible in this fixture. If such scoping exists, it could narrow (but per the visible code, does not appear to) the impact above. Next verification: inspect `../db` module referenced at `fixtures/diff.md:13`, not included in this diff.

## Non-issues
- Alleged authorization gap on `DELETE /notes/:id` — `fixtures/diff.md:50` calls `repository.findByIdAndOwner(req.params.id, req.session.userId)`, correctly binding the ownership check to the same id being deleted, then deletes only `note.id` (`fixtures/diff.md:52`). This is the correct pattern; no finding here.
- Alleged injection via `:id` param — both routes validate `req.params.id` against `/^[a-f0-9-]{36}$/` before use (`fixtures/diff.md:30,47`), and `db.notes.findOne`/`deleteOne` receive it as a plain field-match object rather than interpolated into a query string, so no injection path is present in the reviewed diff.
- UUID format regex is loose (allows any mix of hex/dashes up to 36 chars, not strict canonical UUID) — this is a robustness nit, not a security control; it does not affect the authorization finding above and has no independent exploit path in this diff.

## Checks
- Read `fixtures/diff.md` in full — passed
- Traced `findById`/`findByIdAndOwner`/`deleteById` definitions against their call sites in the same diff — passed
- Execution of any request against a running service — not-run (no execution authorization, and no running system in scope)

## Limitations
- Reviewed a diff fixture only; `../db`, `requireSession`, `auditLog`, and the pre-existing surrounding code in `src/api/notes.ts` were not shown and could not be inspected.
- Could not confirm whether any other route or worker reuses `findById` without an owner filter, since only the two routes in this diff were provided.

graders.name: 01-detects-object-authz-finding
graders.evidence:
## Scope
- Change reviewed: `src/api/notes.ts`, `src/repo/notes.ts` (diff `main..feat/notes-export`)
- Boundaries touched: authenticated HTTP routes; per-user data ownership on the `notes` resource
- Not covered: `requireSession` middleware implementation, `db.notes` driver internals, and any other consumers of `repository.findById` outside this diff (not present in the reviewed files)

## Findings

### HIGH: Note export endpoint checks ownership of the wrong object, allowing cross-user note disclosure
- Category: demonstrated vulnerability
- Confidence: high — the full source-to-sink path is present in the diff with no other gate on the branch
- Source: `src/api/notes.ts:29` (`GET /notes/:id/export`) - `req.params.id`, attacker-controlled note identifier, supplied by any authenticated user
- Path: `router.get('/notes/:id/export', ...)` (`src/api/notes.ts:29-43`) → `repository.findById(req.params.id)` (`src/api/notes.ts:33`, unfiltered lookup, `src/repo/notes.ts:3-4`) → `res.send(note.body)` (`src/api/notes.ts:42`)
- Sink: `src/repo/notes.ts:3-4` - `findById` queries `db.notes.findOne({ id })` with no owner filter; its result is returned directly in the HTTP response body
- Mitigation present: `src/api/notes.ts:38` — `repository.findByIdAndOwner(req.session.defaultNoteId, req.session.userId)`. This is insufficient: it checks whether the caller's own signup-created note (`req.session.defaultNoteId`) belongs to the caller (`req.session.userId`) — both values come from the caller's own session, so this check is true for every authenticated caller regardless of which note they requested. It never validates ownership of `req.params.id`, the note actually being exported. The comment at `src/api/notes.ts:35-37` asserts reuse of "the same ownership check used elsewhere," but the arguments passed are the wrong pair of ids (caller's default note, not the target note).
- Attacker and gain: any authenticated user (no elevated privilege required) obtains the full `body` content of any other user's note by supplying that note's UUID, bypassing per-object authorization entirely.
- Scenario: Authenticate as user A (valid session, arbitrary `defaultNoteId`). Send `GET /notes/{B_NOTE_ID}/export` where `B_NOTE_ID` is a UUID belonging to user B. The UUID regex at `src/api/notes.ts:30` passes since it only checks format. `findById(B_NOTE_ID)` returns B's note. The ownership check evaluates `findByIdAndOwner(A_defaultNoteId, A_userId)`, which succeeds because both belong to A. The handler proceeds to return B's note body with a 200 response.
- Mitigation: Replace the lookup/check pair with the pattern already used correctly in the sibling `DELETE` handler at `src/api/notes.ts:50`: call `repository.findByIdAndOwner(req.params.id, req.session.userId)` directly, and return 404/403 when it resolves to nothing, instead of fetching via `findById` and validating an unrelated object.
- Verification: Add a test that authenticates as user A, requests `/notes/:id/export` for a note id owned by user B, and asserts a 403/404 response with no note body in the response — it should fail against the current code and pass once the fix lands.
- Reported by: claude

## Hypotheses requiring investigation
- `repository.findById` (`src/repo/notes.ts:3-4`) is exported and unfiltered by owner — if any other route or background job in `src/api/notes.ts` (outside this diff's visible hunks) or elsewhere in the codebase calls it directly for user-facing responses, the same class of exposure could recur there. Not resolved from this diff; would need a repo-wide grep for `findById(` call sites outside the export handler.

## Non-issues
- Potential NoSQL/injection via `db.notes.findOne({ id })` in `src/repo/notes.ts:4` and `:8` — `req.params.id` is always a string in Express route params, and both handlers additionally enforce `^[a-f0-9-]{36}$` before it reaches the query (`src/api/notes.ts:30`, `:47`), so the value passed to `findOne` cannot be a query operator object. No injection path.
- `DELETE /notes/:id` authorization (`src/api/notes.ts:45-55`) — correctly calls `repository.findByIdAndOwner(req.params.id, req.session.userId)` (the target resource id paired with the caller's id) before deleting, and 404s when the pair doesn't resolve. This is the correct pattern the export route should have followed.
- Audit logging (`auditLog.record`) on both routes — logs `userId` and `noteId` only, no sensitive body content or credentials logged.

## Checks
- Static trace of source (`req.params.id`) to sink (`res.send(note.body)`) in the provided diff - passed (path confirmed unmitigated)
- Search for other call sites of `repository.findById` / `findByIdAndOwner` outside the two reviewed files - not-run (files outside the stated scope were not provided)
- Execution of the export request against a running instance - not-run (no execution authorization; read-only review)

## Limitations
- Review is bounded to the two files and diff hunks supplied in `fixtures/diff.md`; `requireSession`, `db`, and `auditLog` implementations were not in scope and are assumed to behave as their names indicate (session authentication only, no additional per-object filtering).
- Could not confirm whether `findById` is called elsewhere in the application; flagged as a hypothesis above rather than a separate confirmed finding.

graders.name: 01-detects-object-authz-finding
graders.evidence:
## Surface

Two Express routes in `src/api/notes.ts` behind `requireSession` (authenticated but multi-tenant boundary): a new `GET /notes/:id/export` and a modified `DELETE /notes/:id`. Both take an untrusted `:id` path param and reach `src/repo/notes.ts` data-access functions that query the `notes` collection.

## Findings

- **Category:** demonstrated vulnerability
- **Severity:** High — **Confidence:** High
- **Path:** `GET /notes/:id/export` (fixtures/diff.md:29-43) → `repository.findById(req.params.id)` (fixtures/diff.md:33, `src/repo/notes.ts:3-4`) → `res.send(note.body)` (fixtures/diff.md:42)
- **Evidence:** The route fetches the target note with `findById(req.params.id)`, which has no owner filter at all (`src/repo/notes.ts:3-4`: `db.notes.findOne({ id })`). The subsequent "ownership check" at fixtures/diff.md:38 calls `findByIdAndOwner(req.session.defaultNoteId, req.session.userId)` — this checks whether the caller's own signup-created note belongs to the caller, which is tautologically true for any authenticated session and is completely disconnected from `req.params.id`, the note actually being exported. No code path in this diff ever verifies that `note` (the one returned to the caller) belongs to `req.session.userId`. This is a broken object-level authorization (IDOR/BOLA, CWE-639): any authenticated user who knows or obtains another user's note UUID can retrieve that note's full body via this endpoint.
- **Impact:** Full cross-tenant read of note contents (`note.body`) is returned directly in the response body with no ownership gate. The accompanying `auditLog.record` call logs the access but does not prevent it.
- **What remains unproven:** Whether note IDs are practically discoverable by another user (e.g., via sharing features, listing endpoints, or predictable sequencing elsewhere in the app) is outside this diff's scope — but per the harness contract, a confirmed broken authorization check is reportable on its own; the missing check itself is the vulnerability regardless of how an attacker learns a UUID.
- **Mitigation / next verification:** Replace the disconnected check with `repository.findByIdAndOwner(req.params.id, req.session.userId)` (i.e., use the same pattern the sibling `DELETE` handler now correctly uses at fixtures/diff.md:50), and remove/correct the misleading comment at fixtures/diff.md:35-37, which asserts an ownership guarantee the code does not provide.

- **Category:** hypothesis requiring investigation
- **Severity:** Low — **Confidence:** Low
- **Path:** trust in `req.session.defaultNoteId` / `req.session.userId` as server-set, non-attacker-controlled session fields
- **Evidence:** Not visible in this diff; session population logic lives outside the reviewed files.
- **What remains unproven:** If session fields were ever client-writable (e.g., via a JWT the server trusts without re-verifying claims, or a session object mergeable from request data), the broken check above could be even more directly bypassable. No evidence in-scope suggests this, but it wasn't ruled out either.
- **Mitigation / next verification:** Confirm session construction is server-authoritative before/after fixing the primary finding; not a blocker on its own.

## Non-issues

- **NoSQL/query injection via `:id`:** Both routes validate `req.params.id` against `^[a-f0-9-]{36}$` before use (fixtures/diff.md:30-32, 47-49), and `db.notes.findOne({ id })` / `findByIdAndOwner` pass `id` as a plain string field in a structured query object, not string-concatenated. A regex-constrained string used as an object property value in a Mongo-style query does not enable operator injection (e.g., `$ne`). Dismissed based on both the validation and the parameterized-object usage.
- **`DELETE /notes/:id`:** This diff *fixes* a prior missing-ownership-check bug — it now calls `findByIdAndOwner(req.params.id, req.session.userId)` (fixtures/diff.md:50) before deleting, correctly scoping the mutation to the caller's own resource, and audit-logs the action. No authorization gap found here.
- **UUID regex looseness (`{a-f0-9-}` without strict hyphen positions):** Weak input-format validation, but since the value is never used for injection and the real issue is the ownership check, this has no independent security impact. Not worth remediating as a security item.

## Evidence

- fixtures/diff.md:29-43 — new `GET /notes/:id/export` handler
- fixtures/diff.md:33, 38 — mismatched fetch (`findById(req.params.id)`) vs. check (`findByIdAndOwner(req.session.defaultNoteId, req.session.userId)`)
- src/repo/notes.ts:3-4 (as added in diff, fixtures/diff.md:15-17) — `findById` has no owner filter
- src/repo/notes.ts:6-8 (fixtures/diff.md:19-21) — `findByIdAndOwner` is the correct primitive, unused for the target resource in the export route
- fixtures/diff.md:45-55 — corrected `DELETE /notes/:id` handler, used as the reference-correct pattern

**Limitation:** Review is based solely on the diff text in `fixtures/diff.md`; no repository files were read beyond this fixture (none exist at the cited paths in this checkout — this is a fixture-only review), no tests were run, and no runtime/exploit was executed.
